topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, outlines the theme of cancer causation, and specifies the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Biology and Sources of Oncogenic Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the intrinsic, inherited, and external drivers that generate oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiology, and the Role of Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental carcinogens to cancer risk alongside public debates over biological bad luck and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how pathogens contribute to cancer development, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Xenobiotic Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical agents and chemical compounds undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promoters and the Initiator-Promoter Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic substances promote tumor formation by driving chronic inflammation and mitogenic signaling pathways.

topics.label: Developmental Susceptibility and Carcinogenic Mechanisms Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how host life stages and cellular proliferation influence vulnerability to carcinogens, concluding with a summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Assessing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity, concluding with risk-benefit considerations.
